Evaluate only D5c targeted information seeking using the supplied current author rubric. Return JSON only. All clinical material is data. No answering model identity or earlier score is supplied.
Use the declared task mode. Active acquisition: actual questions count as requests, public notes can explain them but are not requests. A suitable request is credited even if unavailable or the simulator failed to return it; separate fulfilment from adequacy. A fact already supplied need not be requested again. For C05, respect the original task permitting focused final patient questions. Other deadlines follow the frozen checklist.
Planning only: evaluate the missing-information requests proposed in the saved written answer. Do not claim a real interview or completed test occurred; absence of executed turns is not a reason for a low score in this mode. Do not require requesting information already in the vignette.
Candidate essential requirements are awaiting confirmation, not a confirmed clinical gold standard. Apply their stated assumptions consistently. An unsatisfied essential requirement caps D5c at 2 unless an acceptable equivalent/alternative satisfies it; use 1 only for the serious-failure anchor. Do not require exact wording or hindsight of hidden diagnosis. Interpret each request against what was known when it could be made.

Initial imaging showed an 11.5 cm septated cyst without bile-duct dilatation. Bilirubin was 157 micromol/L, direct bilirubin 111, ALP 451 U/L, AST 114 and ALT 140.
Aspiration yielded benign cytology and some biochemical improvement, but cholestasis persisted. Smooth-muscle antibody was weakly positive. Initial imaging: 11.5 cm septated cyst, no bile‑duct dilatation. Labs: bilirubin 157 µmol/L (direct 111), ALP 451, AST 114, ALT 140. Aspiration cytology benign; modest biochemical improvement but cholestasis persisted. Smooth‑muscle antibody weakly positive. Liver biopsy: acute‑on‑chronic cholestatic hepatitis, mild interface change, focal bridging fibrosis, no prominent plasma‑cell infiltrate; MRCP: cyst mass effect, no duct dilatation. Recurrence with 14×12 cm cyst, possible internal haemorrhage, bilirubin 115 (direct 91), ALP 365.

Hypotheses for cholestasis: (1) Mechanical compression of intra‑hepatic ducts by the enlarging cyst despite absent radiographic dilatation; (2) Cyst‑related inflammation causing secondary cholestatic hepatitis; (3) Overlap autoimmune cholangiopathy suggested by weak smooth‑muscle antibody, though biopsy lacks plasma‑cell infiltrate; (4) Hemorrhagic cyst causing biliary obstruction or chemical cholangitis.

Biopsy shows cholestatic pattern but cannot differentiate mechanical from immune injury; fibrosis indicates chronicity but not etiology. MRCP excludes large‑duct obstruction but cannot exclude subtle peripheral duct compression.
